name: אֲחַזְיָהוּ
summary: Two kings. Ahaziah son of Ahab, king of Israel, who fell through the lattice of his upper room and sent to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, and died by the word of Yahweh through Elijah (1Ki 22:40, 52; 2Ki 1:2–17); Jehoshaphat joined him in building ships, and they were broken (2Ch 20:35–37). And Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, son of Athaliah, who went down to see Joram at Jezreel and was killed by Jehu (2Ki 8:24–29; 9:16–29; 2Ch 22:1–9), after which Athaliah destroyed the royal seed but his son Joash was hidden (2Ki 11:1–2); he is also called Jehoahaz (2Ch 21:17) and Azariah (2Ch 22:6). The short form אַחְזַי, Ahzai, is borne by a priest's ancestor (Neh 11:13). The name is the verb אָחַז with יָהוּ, “Yahweh has taken hold”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah (אֲחַזְיָהוּ) his son reigned in his place.”
Ahaziah fell through the lattice and sent to inquire of Baal-zebub.
“He died according to the word of Yahweh which Elijah had spoken.”
“Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.”
Jehu pursued him: “strike him too in the chariot”.
They buried him, “for he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought Yahweh with all his heart”.
Athaliah saw that her son was dead and destroyed the royal seed; Jehosheba stole Joash son of Ahaziah away.
The same king called יְהוֹאָחָז, Jehoahaz, the same two parts in the other order.
“Amashsai son of Azarel son of אַחְזַי son of Meshillemoth son of Immer.”

note: Takes a.cl.ad (38 tokens), which includes the short form אַחְזַי, Ahzai, of Neh 11:13. TIPNR lists אַחְזַי among the forms of Meshullam@1Ch.9.12 (its parallel 1Ch 9:12 has Jahzerah son of Meshullam), so that record is tagged here; its own name Meshullam is not filed under a.cl.ad, so the word sheet shows this entry only at Neh 11:13. Review whether Ahzai should rather be its own name entry. TIPNR keys Ahaziah of Judah as Ahaziah@2Ki.8.24, with the forms Jehoahaz and Azariah.
